CHIEF COMPLAINT
Followup of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male presenting for followup of his depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension. He reports that the past year and a half has been challenging, with anxiety and stress related to holiday preparations. He had a nice Thanksgiving seeing family after about two years, though it was stressful and involved a lot of work. He is planning to take a vacation somewhere warm in the new year. Regarding his depression, he tried a new strategy over the summer by taking long walks outside every morning, which he enjoyed due to the nice weather and blooming plants. This also encouraged weekend yard work and physical activity. However, with the changing seasons and cold weather, he has been unable to continue this routine and needs to find alternative strategies. He denies being ready to try medications at this time and is interested in exploring alternative options. He denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. Regarding diabetes management, he did okay through Halloween but did not stick closely to his diet during Thanksgiving week, though he reports it has improved since then and he is monitoring intake. For his hypertension, he purchased a blood pressure cuff as recommended and reports readings have been moderate with nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, blood in stool, or weight loss. Review of systems sheet completed at check-in.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin
Lisinopril

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys outdoor activities including walking and yard work. Recently took time off for holiday gatherings. Currently planning vacation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well-controlled.
Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated.
Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base (previously noted). Regular rate and rhythm otherwise.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in lower extremities.

RESULTS
EKG: No concerning findings; appropriate for patient's age and risk factors.
Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0% (elevated; goal <6%).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy/counseling. Patient not currently interested in pharmacotherapy. Continue monitoring for suicidal/homicidal ideation.
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8%. Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Order repeat hemoglobin A1C in couple of months. Order lipid panel.
3. Hypertension: Blood pressure well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order echocardiogram to recheck cardiac status given systolic ejection murmur.
